thread:
incidents_bot: :rotating_light: Incident alert: elevated 5xx and tail latency on /v1/generate for model variant v4-experimental across us-west-2. Pager routed to oncall amaia_oncall and eng-sre.
erica_ops: seeing a spike in tokens and retries; cost alarms also triggered. Some requests are timing out after retries. Can we confirm if it's inference timeouts or upstream queuing?
julia_sre: checking runtime logs now. Early signs point to repeated KV cache thrashing when seq_len > 1024 on v4-experimental after the latest kernel pick. Also higher memory churn on a subset of GPU hosts.
kevin_support: flagging PROD customer stacklytics (customer-id: cust_84a) reporting errors in their webhooks and increased latency. Their traffic is heavy, but shouldn't be hitting this level of tail errors.
amaia_oncall: acknowledged. I'll gather traces and start mitigations. Paging product_olivia for customer comms. @erica_ops can you identify the variant routing policy for heavy keys (we might throttle or roll back)?
erica_ops: current routing: 15% traffic -> v4-experimental (canary) via weighted routing, rest -> v3-stable. Some high-QPS API keys were included in the canary bucket due to recent key tag changes. I'm preparing a quick list.
incidents_bot: channel #incidents created. Severity: Sev2. Runbook: confirm impact, mitigate traffic, assign owners, post customer note.
sam_r: two quick options: 1) temporarily disable v4-experimental from routing (set weight=0) — immediate but blunt, or 2) patch kernel fallback on runtime hosts — riskier. Recommend option 1 for safety and to restore service quickly.
amaia_oncall: Agreed. Let's shelve the canary. erica, can you make the change and list the exact API call so support/product can reference it for the incident timeline?
erica_ops: doing it now. API call I'll run via internal controlplane: curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal.redwood/api/v1/variants/route" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-v4","variant":"v4-experimental","weight":0}'
(erica_ops executes)
erica_ops: change applied. Confirmed: v4-experimental weight set to 0 across all regions. Rolling window routing now back to v3-stable and v4-beta where applicable. Monitoring.
julia_sre: metrics: 5xx dropped ~83% in the last 2m. Latency returning to baseline. Good call.
kevin_support: started customer outreach template for impacted customers: short note acknowledging throttling/errors, we disabled a canary variant and are restoring stable routing; next update in 30m. Posting to stacklytics.
product_olivia: prepping a concise message: "We've temporarily removed experimental model variant from serving after detecting elevated error rates; your requests are currently served by the stable variant. We're monitoring and will follow up with timeline and root cause." Will send after we confirm stability.
amaia_oncall: quick impact assessment: using sampling we see ~220 keys hit the canary in the last hour, of which 6 are high-QPS (>=200 rps). Only 2 customers are showing client-visible errors: stacklytics and nimbus-ai. Others saw increased latency but requests completed.
sam_r: we should also check quota and rate-limit responses. If some keys retried aggressively they might have tripped quota protections causing churn. Consider temporarily increasing quota for affected keys to avoid cascading errors while we verify.
erica_ops: I can perform a selective quota bump for the two affected customers for 30 minutes: via admin console -> API keys -> cust_84a and cust_99e -> set concurrency limit +50% and token rate +20%. Will do after confirming authorization.
kevin_support: customer approval? I have ok from stacklytics on temporary mitigation - they prefer us to avoid throttling them while they investigate client retries. Nimbus is OK with temporary lift too.
(erica_ops executes quota updates)
erica_ops: quota updates applied to cust_84a and cust_99e. Documenting change in incident log.
julia_sre: note: we should not expand quota globally. This is a targeted mitigation only. Also recommend adding a short-term traffic-shaping rule to deprioritize experimental variant traffic for keys that didn't opt-in to canary to avoid surprises.
amaia_oncall: good point. erica, can you add a temporary traffic policy that redirects any key not tagged "canary_opt_in" off experimental variants? That will prevent accidental inclusion.
erica_ops: adding policy now. Rule: if tag != canary_opt_in -> variant weight override = 0 for v4-experimental. Applying via controlplane policy API.
erica_ops: policy applied. Verified with test key — routing ignores experimental variant as expected.
sam_r: next steps: 1) keep v4-experimental weight at 0 until kernel fix lands, 2) continue monitoring 15m, 3) postmortem owner: eng-ml (julia_sre + infra lead) for root cause, 4) communicate to customers.
incidents_bot: reminder: on-call handoff scheduled in 45m. Current oncall: amaia_oncall. Next oncall: julia_sre (escrow). Please record status and outstanding actions before handoff.
amaia_oncall: preparing handoff note: service stabilized, v4-experimental shelved, quotas temporarily adjusted for two customers, traffic-policy added to prevent further accidental canary routing. Outstanding: kernel regression analysis, confirm if KV cache tuning avoids thrash.
product_olivia: sent customer notifications to stacklytics + nimbus and to general impacted-customer list. Copy of message in #support-private.
kevin_support: both customers acknowledged and are monitoring. No escalations to sales yet.
julia_sre: I'll take over next oncall and coordinate with eng-runtime and eng-ml. Initial hypothesis: kernel pick combined with longer sequences caused repeated cache invalidations which triggered memory compaction and OOM-retries. We'll reproduce in staging with seq_len=1536 and high concurrency.
erica_ops: saving the routing change + policy + quota modifications in the incident record (inc-2026-03-15-184550). Linking logs and host IDs.
amaia_oncall: quick ask: can someone capture a list of keys that were unexpectedly in canary? erica, you mentioned 220; please add a CSV to the incident doc.
erica_ops: uploaded keys-list.csv to the incident binder. Also added timeline with exact API commands executed and timestamps.
incidents_bot: action items created: #1 reproduce in staging (owner: julia_sre), #2 kernel fallback patch (owner: eng-runtime lead), #3 detailed customer impact writeup (owner: product_olivia), #4 postmortem draft due in 72h (owner: eng-ml).
amaia_oncall: handing off to julia_sre in 10. Status: stable, mitigations applied, monitoring green but we're not closing yet. If anything flares up during handoff ping me.
julia_sre: taking over. Thanks all. I'll sync with runtime leads and keep customer comms loops open. Adding a note to avoid re-enabling canary until we validate the kernel selection and add a canary gating test for seq_len > 1024.
kevin_support: closing loop once postmortem and customer-facing RCA ready.
product_olivia: planning to send a follow-up update in 90m with a short technical note + ETA for RCA.
incidents_bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update in 30m or on change. Severity remains Sev2 until postmortem complete.
